summary.headline: Regaal Resources posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹232 million (+38.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.1%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 manufacturing revenue rose about 64% YoY to ₹3,141 million, and value add rose 64.3% to ₹1,290 million at a 40.8% value-add margin. Operating EBITDA grew 54.7% to ₹542 million, and PAT reached a record ₹232 million at a 7.3% margin. Maize crushing volume was 90,489 MT, up 32% YoY, despite a roughly one-month disruption after damage to a 10 MW turbine at the newly commissioned A25 facility, which has since been recommissioned. Net debt rose to ₹8,808 million on working capital build-up from advance maize procurement, which management expects to unwind over the next two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +64% YoY vs ₹1,916 million in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: ₹5,357 million term loan; ₹3,506 million working capital

segments.name: Co-manufacturing / manufacturing
segments.commentary: Manufacturing revenue ₹3,141 million, up 64% YoY; crushing 90,489 MT in Q2, up 32% YoY. Products include starch, gluten/feed, germ, fibre and liquid glucose.

segments.name: Trading (maize)
segments.commentary: Management said trading sales in Q2 FY26 were negligible; in Q2 FY27 trading sales were about ₹127 million against ₹1,927 million manufacturing (described as opportunistic, low margin around 5-6%).

segments.name: Value-added products (dextrose, modified starch, CMS, oxidised starch)
segments.commentary: Liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines commissioned; modified starch line started. Value-added share guided at 10-11% in FY27 and 20-23% in FY28 (excluding liquid glucose).

guidance_outlook: Interest cost for FY27 guided at about ₹40-42 crore (H1 at ₹20-22 crore); management said it will not exceed budget.
H2 FY27 crushing guided at about 2,040,000 MT, implying FY27 volume of about 4,040,000 MT.
Working capital debt expected to fall materially by March 2027 as inventory is consumed; CWIP-linked term loans to be repaid as projects complete.
Starch-linked sustainable margin framed at about ₹4,500/MT; Q2 EBITDA per tonne about ₹6,000 and H1 about ₹5,300 per tonne.
Maize inventory covers H2 requirements (about 90% in plant), with stock expected to last to about mid-March 2027.
Value-added capex about 27.5% (approx. ₹275 crore) yet to be capitalised; additional 1.6 MW power plant using methane from effluent treatment planned; DMSO-type product planned around FY28.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity expanded to 1,650 MT/day; operating at 1,500-1,575 MT/day in the recent period, with 1,600 MT/day achieved per management.
A25 facility's 10 MW turbine damaged in Q2, causing about one month's closure; recommissioned and now fully operational.
Liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines commissioned; modified starch (CMS, oxidised starch) started, with sampling and customer approvals underway.
Around 65% of planned capex is said to be already deployed, with the balance (roughly ₹275 crore) to be capitalised in FY27-FY28.
Land: about 70 acres signed with farmers; 57 acres of land said to be vacant at the Bihar site for future expansion.
demand_pricing: Maize prices up about 50% from ₹10 to ₹15/kg (per management) over the period; starch realisations about ₹49-51/kg, germ ₹83 from ₹60, fibre ₹23 from ₹16, and gluten ₹64-65 from ₹60.
Management said order intake reached about 150% of target and prices were being raised again after the call.
Exports about 10% of starch and fibre volumes; management cited tapioca starch at about $700/t.
Distributor sales reduced significantly; management prioritises dealer/retail channels.
GST recovery from distributors: about 60% recovered, with the balance expected by December 2026.
Average realisation for the quarter about ₹35/kg per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q2 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher capacity lowering fixed cost per tonne, higher conversion spread, higher selling prices, and new export markets.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital debt come down over the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital debt will fall by March as the high-cost maize inventory is consumed; interest cost is expected to stay within the ₹40-42 crore budget.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 H2 volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 crushing guided at about 2,040,000 MT, giving FY27 total of about 4,040,000 MT; management said the turbine outage cost about 20,000 MT.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin when maize costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current maize inventory was bought at about ₹30-31/kg versus about ₹34 cost, with starch at ₹49-51/kg; sustainability was framed around ₹4,500/MT, but no firm guidance was given beyond FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further capex plans beyond the current expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on stabilising current capacity; a 1.6 MW methane-based power plant and an additional product are planned, with timing around FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trading share and long-term intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trading is opportunistic (about ₹8.5 crore in October) and not a long-term vision.

risks_watch: Maize procurement cost reset: Q3-Q4 inventory bought at about ₹30-31/kg is being consumed, with fresh procurement expected to be at higher prices from mid-March 2027.
Value-added ramp: management said real value-add data will only show in Q3 and full picture in Q4; customer approvals still in progress.
Ethanol-linked maize diversion and crop shortfalls in some states may tighten availability, per management.
Execution risk: earlier turbine failure shows plant reliability risk at the new A25 facility.
Debt reduction and interest cost trajectory against guidance of ₹40-42 crore for FY27 (H1 at ₹20-22 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, margins and debt reduction, but evasive on specific value-add figures, margin sustainability and future capex, deferring details to later quarters. Several answers were vague or contradictory on figures (for example, the balance of value-added capex and the margin-per-tonne basis), so the numbers should be verified against the filings.
key_quotes: We also achieved our highest ever quarterly profit after tax of 232 million, accompanied by a record path margin of 7.3%.
The turbine has been successfully recommissioned and the facility is now fully operational.
As the inventory is progressively consumed over the next two quarters, working capital requirements and associated borrowings are expected to moderate.
It will whatever we had given you basically think guidance can be this 40, 40, 42, 38 whatever we have told you it will be staying there.

adds.what: Crushing capacity expanded to 1,650 MT/day (operating 1,500-1,575 MT/day; 1,600 MT/day achieved)
Liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines
Modified starch (CMS, oxidised starch) line, in sampling and customer approvals
Balance of value-added capex (~Rs 275 crore, ~27.5%) to be capitalised in FY27-FY28
Additional 1.6 MW methane-based power plant from effluent treatment

growth.why: Management guides FY27 crushing to about 4.04m t (H2 ~2.04m t, implying ~8% growth on Q2's 32% pace) and FY28 crushing to 525,000-550,000 t, backed by 1,650 MT/day crushing capacity and commissioned liquid glucose/dextrose lines, though the ~Rs 275 crore value-added capex is still being capitalised over FY27-FY28 and there are no firm order or contract figures behind the volume guide.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA ~Rs 6,000/t vs H1 ~Rs 5,300/t and sustainable starch margin framed at ~Rs 4,500/t; maize inventory bought at Rs 30-31/kg vs ~Rs 34 cost, but fresh procurement expected at higher prices from mid-March 2027, so margin expansion is likely to be uneven and not firmly guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Balance ~Rs 275 crore (~27.5%) of value-added capex is under construction and to be capitalised in FY27-FY28, with crushing capacity already at 1,650 MT/day and running 1,500-1,575 MT/day (~1,600 achieved), so ~5-10% headroom is used up soon after.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 crushing ~2,040,000 MT (FY27 ~4,040,000 MT) and FY28 525,000-550,000 MT, but Q2's 90,489 MT already includes a turbine outage costing ~20,000 MT and no firm order book figures were given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at roughly 1,500-1,600 MT/day against 1,650 MT/day capacity (~90%+) with a 1.6 MW methane power plant and a DMSO-type product planned around FY28, but management deferred further capex detail to later quarters and said focus is on stabilising current capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 crushing guide was raised to ~4.04m t and management said order intake reached ~150% of target and prices are being raised again, but H1 value-add data only shows in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Maize cost reset from mid-March 2027, ethanol-linked diversion and state-level crop shortfalls may tighten availability, and A25 turbine failure (about one month closure, ~20,000 MT lost) shows plant reliability risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Modified starch (CMS, oxidised starch) line is in trial runs with customer approvals underway, and liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines are already commissioned, but value-add revenue only shows from Q3 and the full picture in Q4.

rows.label: Working capital debt unwind by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt rose to Rs 8,808 million on advance maize buying (Rs 3,506 million working capital debt) and management expects it to fall as inventory is consumed, with cash conversion cycle already down to 123 days from 130.

rows.label: Price increases after the call
rows.why: Management said prices were being raised again after the call and order intake reached ~150% of target, with starch realisations ~Rs 49-51/kg and maize up ~50% from Rs 10 to Rs 15/kg.

rows.label: Export expansion
rows.why: Exports are only ~10% of starch and fibre volumes, and management cited new export markets and tapioca starch at ~$700/t as a supportive price reference, but no export target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, margins and debt reduction and on order intake, but evasive on value-add figures, margin sustainability beyond FY28 and further capex; analysts pushed on margin per tonne basis and the balance of value-added capex.
